new_statements.quote: 17. — WAMOANG. Aire : Plaine de Voh, occupée aujourd'hui par la ville européenne. 3 indigènes. [...] § 2. — Accent et ton. le = nous, bas / le = eux, haut.
new_statements.translation: 17. — Wamoang. Area: the Voh plain, today occupied by the European town. 3 natives. [...] § 2. — Accent and tone. le = we, low / le = they, high.
new_statements.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie. Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie (Travaux et Mémoires de l'Institut d'Ethnologie XLVI). Chapter '17. — Wamoang', pp. 111-117.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Checked the page images themselves, not only the scanned. (printed p. 111, running head "GROUPE DU NORD : WAMOANG") shows "17. — WAMOANG ¹." then "AIRE : Plaine de Voh, occupée aujourd'hui par la ville européenne. 3 indigènes.", then "I PHONÉTIQUE. § 1. — Transcription." with a consonant/vowel table and "Le g est très rare, et semble appartenir aux dialectes voisins."; footnote 1: "Wamoang signifie : qu'y a-t-il ? quoi ? comme le jiè en AJIË." p. 112) opens with "§ 2. — Accent et ton." followed by exactly two centred lines "le = nous, bas" / "le = eux, haut." and then "II MOTS. § 3. Les mots se terminent par une voyelle ou une consonne..." — so the quoted passage is there verbatim (the only…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for stress placement is given. The entire 'Accent et ton' section for Wamoang is a single minimal pair in which the 1pl inclusive pronoun le is said to be pronounced with low pitch and the 3pl pronoun le with high pitch, i.e. a lexical pitch (tone) contrast is noted; Voegelin & Voegelin 1964: 63 restate this second-hand as 'vowels occur with at least two phonemic distinctions of tone'. No accent diacritic is used in the Wamoang wordlists and the position of word stress is never stated.
new_statements.exceptions: none; note that Rivierre 1972 (BSLP 67: 302, on file under cemu1238) classes the surviving Voh-Koné dialects as 'dialectes sans tons', so Leenhardt's single pitch pair should not be read as evidence of a tone system
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated pronoun forms (word level) from a questionnaire-based sketch made when the language had 3 speakers; Leenhardt's general phonetics chapter (p. 11) defers 'l'accent, le ton' to each language chapter, and for Wamoang that chapter offers only this pair.
new_statements.identity_note: Waamwang = Leenhardt's 'Wamoang' (his no. 17), the dialect of the Voh plain; Glottolog waam1236 / ISO wmn; a member of the Voh-Koné dialect cluster (Bwatoo bwat1240, Haeke haek1239, Haveke have1241, Hmwaveke hmwa1243, Vamale vama1243). Extinct: 3 speakers in 1939 (Leenhardt 1946: 111), 'quasi-extinct' in the 1940s (Rohleder 2024), 'éteint' (Rivierre, Corpus de la parole); ISO CR 2012-143 (rejected) proposed folding it into Haveke [hvk]. The quoted statement is the sole first-hand description ever made.

Refs: Leenhardt 1946 (only MED source), Haudricourt 1971 overview, ISO CR 2012-143; Ethnologue 2025 status 10 Extinct; alt name Wamoang. No grammar/phonology exists.

sources.citation: Rohleder, Jean. 2024. A grammar of Vamale. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Waamwang 'quasi-extinct' in the 1940s; appears only in a Leenhardt-based pronoun table (3.2) and the Voh-Koné tree (Fig. 3.13). §5.6 Stress is Vamale-only (penultimate); nothing on Waamwang.

sources.note: No mention of Waamwang; only a general remark that non-tonal Kanak neighbours of the tone languages 'marquent des accents en particulier sur la première syllabe (Moyse-Faurie, 2018)'.
